profile.headline: Senior Software Engineer | Security Engineer & Reverse Engineer | Malware Analysis, Adversarial ML
profile.summary:
I'm a security engineer and senior software engineer with an active Top Secret clearance. Most of my work sits at the overlap of cybersecurity, software engineering, and machine learning.
 
I spent five years at Georgia Tech Research Institute as a Machine Learning Security Engineer. A lot of that time went into a Python malware analysis platform: static and dynamic analysis, byte-entropy, CFGs, packing detection, network traffic, and matching function hashes against known malicious patterns. I did reverse engineering of embedded systems in Ghidra, trained a PyTorch Geometric GNN to flag malicious JavaScript from ASTs, helped build an adversarial ML testbed, and wrote a Rust/AWS honeypot. I also worked on OSINT ingest systems in Java (Apache Storm, Elasticsearch, Neo4j, MongoDB) and a LangChain plus local LLM setup for packet analysis.
 
At Thompson Software Solutions I started on SBOM vulnerability scanning and automated remediation for embedded Yocto systems. Currently I'm on C# / ASP.NET flight-avionics software: SignalR, multithreaded backends, and hardening API endpoints.
 
Tools I use a lot: Python, C/C++, Rust, Java, C#, x86/MIPS, Ghidra, IDA, Wireshark, PyTorch, TensorFlow, LangChain, AWS, Docker, Flask, ASP.NET, MongoDB, Elasticsearch, and Neo4j.
 
M.S. in Computer Science from Georgia Tech (Interactive Intelligence). B.S. in Computer Science, Cybersecurity from the University of Georgia, where I did undergrad research in the cybersecurity lab under Dr. Kyu Hyung Lee.
 
Happy to talk about security engineering, reverse engineering, ML for cyber, or software roles that need some mix of those.
